messages:
maya: ran through the new quickstart with a customer. they could make an initial hello call during sign-up, then after they added a payment method the same sample app started returning 402 Payment Required on /v1/generate. UI showed "free credits applied" before payment step. anyone seen this flip?

simon: can you paste the curl and response headers? 402 on first real request after adding card sounds like billing state race.

maya: here you go:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}'
```
response: 402 Payment Required
headers: x-request-id: req_abc123, x-billing-state: pending_verification, x-retry-after: 0
body: {"error":"payment_required","message":"Confirm payment method to continue"}

maya: note: we were handing customer a service account key generated via the onboarding flow. they set env var SAMPLE_API_KEY per the sample app README. i think sample expects REDWOOD_API_KEY though? not sure.

tasha: we've seen two things similar: (1) onboarding creates a temporary org-level credit record while payment verifies, which the console shows as "free credits applied" but backend flags billing state as pending until KYC/processor callback; (2) the sample app's SDK retries non-idempotent generate calls and swallows the follow-up 402, so the first UI appears successful then the next call fails. :thinking:

simon: ah — so behavior could be: initial client call hits a cached route that returns 200 from prefix caching, then subsequent call hits billing enforcement after the processor callback. also SDK retry on 402 would be wrong: 402 should surface immediately. can you confirm which SDK and version the sample app used?

maya: they used js-sdk v1.2.0 (the quickstart template).

simon: v1.2.0 had a retry policy that treated all 4xx as transient unless header `x-no-retry` present. looks like a regression. filed a quick PR in my queue for the retry policy.

maya: also, the env var mismatch — customer had SAMPLE_API_KEY set from README, but the sample app code loads process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY. so they rotated keys and ended up hitting a different workspace token later. that explains the flip for some users. i'll open a docs PR to make names consistent.

tonboard-bot: created INF-4821: "onboarding: sample app billing flip + SDK retries on 402" and assigned to simon. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821

simon: plan: (a) hotfix SDK so 402 is not retried (owner: simon, eta: 3 days), (b) add a small check in quickstart that does a lightweight /v1/status billing check before running the first generate and surfaces friendly message if billing_state != active (owner: devex, eta: next week), (c) docs fix to align env var names (owner: maya, eta: today).

tasha: add a note for support playbook: if customer reports flip, ask for org id, x-request-id, and whether they used the sample template env names. also check processor callback timestamps against first and second request times.

maya: customer workaround: re-generate service key after payment confirmed + restart sample app. that worked. i'll update the quickstart troubleshooting section. :thumbsup:

devex: copying this into the onboarding runbook and flagging for the next RC. thanks for the fast triage.

simon: cc @security — no sensitive PII here but FYI on token handling and env var confusion.

maya: closing loop with the customer now, will paste confirmation here when fixed.
